about: Slackcountry lines reached from ski lifts, for Skiing mode (slackcountry.js). Hand-kept: one entry per resort, with its backcountry gates and lines. Each line's g has ski (the descent), up (from the gate to the top) and out (the way back), as flat [lat, lon, ...]. After changing a line, run node scripts/build-slackcountry.mjs: it adds the steepness, aspects, drop and terrain class estimate (calc) from the terrain tiles. Sources: the resort's backcountry page and trail map, OpenStreetMap (osm = way ids), camptocamp and trip reports linked on each line. approx = drawn from the terrain model, not a GPS track.

resorts.name: Whistler Blackcomb
resorts.emergency: Emergency outside the boundary: 911 (Whistler Search and Rescue). In the ski area: 604-935-5555.
rules: Ski patrol and avalanche control stop at the boundary. Outside it nobody checks the snow, closes slopes or comes to look for you.
Everyone in the group needs an avalanche transceiver (and to know how to use it), a probe, a shovel, skins and a phone.
Check the Terrain Status map before you go out and before you come back in, and respect closures. The gates close when the avalanche danger is high or when there is blasting.
A backcountry ticket gets you up one set of lifts once, and you sign the Backcountry Access Agreement. Uphill travel inside the ski area only on the signed routes.
The terrain past the gates is in Garibaldi Provincial Park.

gates.name: Flute gate
gates.note: At the top of Flute Bowl. Get to Flute from the Symphony, Harmony 6 or Peak Express, then skin or bootpack up Flute Summit (about 15 minutes). Leads into Garibaldi Provincial Park: the Musical Bumps, Oboe and Singing Pass.

gates.name: Garibaldi Park gate (Blackcomb Glacier)
gates.note: On the Blackcomb Glacier, entered from the top of the Showcase T-Bar (experts also come in from Spanky's Ladder). Leads to the East Col and the Spearhead Range. Whistler Blackcomb asks you to recheck the East Col's status the morning of your trip and again just before you go.

gates.name: Backcountry gate by 7th Heaven
gates.note: Marked on the resort's trail map beside Cloud Nine and Panorama, near the bottom of 7th Heaven. Where Body Bag Bowl and DOA come back into the ski area, and where tours up Disease Ridge start.

gates.name: No gate: Khyber's
gates.note: There's no gate here. Skiers leave the boundary from Upper Peak to Creek, by the tiny Stu Inn shelter. The ski area doesn't recommend it, and it isn't controlled or patrolled.

lines.name: Oboe, north side
lines.about: The classic first slackcountry run from Whistler: over Flute and Oboe, then down Oboe's north side, open slopes then trees, to the Singing Pass trail in the Fitzsimmons valley.
lines.access: Through the Flute gate, then east along the Musical Bumps ridge to Oboe Summit (1956 m), on skins or with a short bootpack.
lines.exit: The Singing Pass trail, down the south side of Fitzsimmons Creek to Whistler Village (about 7 km). It can be icy and hard to follow when there's little snow.
hazards: Open avalanche slopes above the trees.
Hard to find the way on the ridge in a whiteout.
Creek gullies near the bottom: a small slide piles up deep there.

lines.name: Oboe, east side
lines.about: Lots of tree lines on the east side of Oboe, the better side of the peak: gentle at first, then steeper and more continuous through the openings at treeline, down to the Singing Pass trail. So popular you often don't need to break trail.
lines.access: Through the Flute gate and east along the Musical Bumps to Oboe Summit (1956 m).
lines.exit: The Singing Pass trail, down the south side of Fitzsimmons Creek to Whistler Village.
hazards: Busy: watch for other groups above you.
Avalanche paths cross the Singing Pass trail on the way out.

lines.name: Flute, the back side to Oboe Creek
lines.about: The first run past the Flute gate: from the boundary at the top of Flute Summit down the far side to Oboe Creek. Gentler slopes far to skier's right, a steady sparsely treed line in the middle, trees to skier's left.
lines.access: The Flute gate at the top of Flute Bowl: skin or bootpack up Flute Summit (about 15 minutes) from the Symphony or Harmony chairs.
lines.exit: Follow Oboe Creek down to the Singing Pass trail and out to Whistler Village. Or skin back up past Lesser Flute into the resort.
hazards: Don't drift too far to skier's right: that drains toward Cheakamus Lake, and many lost parties there have needed Search and Rescue.
Creek gullies near the bottom: a small slide piles up deep there.

lines.name: Musical Bumps to Singing Pass
lines.about: A ridge tour over Flute, Oboe and the Musical Bumps to Singing Pass: mostly gentle, with easy ways back toward the resort early on. Russet Lake and the Kees and Claire Hut are beyond the pass, and it's the west end of the Spearhead Traverse.
lines.access: Through the Flute gate at the top of Flute Bowl.
lines.exit: The Singing Pass trail down to Whistler Village, or skin back over the Bumps to the resort.
hazards: Avalanche hazard on every open slope along the ridge.
Route finding is hard in a whiteout.
About 8 km and 4 hours from the lifts to the pass, then the long trail out: start early.

lines.clsWhy: Mostly a gentle ridge with ways around the steep slopes; the trail out does pass under avalanche paths.

lines.name: Cowboy Ridge
lines.about: Open lines off Cowboy Ridge, past Singing Pass, above the upper Melody Creek. The line drawn is the skier's left one.
lines.access: Through the Flute gate, along the Musical Bumps to Singing Pass, then skin up Cowboy Ridge. It's far from the lifts: plan a full day.
lines.exit: Down to Melody Creek and the Singing Pass trail to Whistler Village, or skin back west over the Musical Bumps to the resort.
hazards: Open alpine slopes with few trees: wind slabs and cornices on the ridge.
A long way from help, with a long exit.

lines.name: Fissile Peak, north-west face
lines.about: The steep peak you see from the village, above Russet Lake: a long, steep descent down its north-west face. A Whistler backcountry classic for strong, fit skiers. Banana Chute and Psycho Chute are on the same face.
lines.access: Through the Flute gate, the long way over the Musical Bumps to Singing Pass and Russet Lake (Kees and Claire Hut), then a steep bootpack up Fissile's west ridge.
lines.exit: Back past Russet Lake to Singing Pass, then the Singing Pass trail to Whistler Village. Many groups sleep at the Kees and Claire Hut.
hazards: Big, steep face (45° and more): any slide is serious.
Cornices and rock on the west ridge bootpack.
Far from help: a full day or more from the lifts.

lines.name: Khyber's (Khyber Ridge)
lines.about: Off Whistler Peak, skier's left of Upper Peak to Creek: steep trees, gullies and cliffs off Khyber Ridge, down toward the Microwave Tower road. It has no gate and no control.
lines.access: Peak Express, then Upper Peak to Creek past Bagel Bowl. Right after an S bend, the trees on skier's left run past the boundary (the tiny Stu Inn shelter sits there).
lines.exit: The Microwave Tower Access Road back to Creekside: about 3 km past the microwave tower, keep right (north-north-east), or you end up at the bottom of Cheakamus Lake Road.
hazards: Don't go more than about 200 m skier's left (south): that drops into the Cheakamus Lake drainage, under very large avalanche paths, with cliff bands and a long, bushy way out.
Very easy to get lost: the terrain confuses even experienced navigators.
Cliffs and creek gullies (terrain traps).

lines.name: Body Bag Bowl
lines.about: A bowl on the south side of Blackcomb Peak, below the East Col and Disease Ridge, that comes back into the ski area near the bottom of 7th Heaven.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate on the Blackcomb Glacier, up to the East Col, then south along the ridge to the top. Or tour up Disease Ridge from the gate near the bottom of 7th Heaven.
lines.exit: Trend skier's right (west) back into the ski area at Lakeside Bowl and ski to the bottom of 7th Heaven.
hazards: Cornices along the ridge at the top.
Sun-warmed slopes in the afternoon: wet slides.

lines.name: DOA (Down, Over and Around)
lines.about: An expert couloir on Blackcomb Peak: a ski-wide choke around a rock at the entrance, then about 220 m between rock walls, up to about 45°.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate on the Blackcomb Glacier, about 150 m to the East Col, then a short climbing traverse south across the east side of Blackcomb Peak to the entry notch.
lines.exit: Where the couloir opens into the bowl, trend skier's right toward the ski area boundary and back to the bottom of 7th Heaven.
hazards: No-fall entrance: a slip in the choke is very serious.
Sunny slope: crust, or wet snow when it warms up.
Gets scraped and bumpy fast after a storm.

lines.name: Disease Ridge, north side
lines.about: A short run (about 60 m) down the north side of Disease Ridge, the ridge south of 7th Heaven, back toward Lakeside Bowl and the bottom of 7th Heaven. A quick lap from the gate.
lines.access: The backcountry gate by 7th Heaven, then skin south up to Disease Ridge. Also reached from the East Col.
lines.exit: Down the gully west to the bottom of 7th Heaven.
hazards: Wind slabs and storm slabs. Avalanches have run here on weak layers low on the ridge.
The gully at the bottom is a terrain trap.

lines.name: Circle Lake bowls
lines.about: South-east facing open slopes from the col south of the Spearhead down to Circle Lake: a long, steady fall line that splits into two broad gullies on either side of a low ridge.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate on the Blackcomb Glacier, then a short traversing climb to the Spearhead col.
lines.exit: Skin over the col between Blackcomb Peak and Disease Ridge to the top of Body Bag Bowl, ski it and come back in at the bottom of 7th Heaven.
hazards: Sunny aspect: slopes warm up fast in the afternoon and in spring.
The two gullies at the bottom are terrain traps.

lines.name: Husume
lines.about: A north-west facing couloir north of the Spearhead: about 250 m of skiing, up to 40°, down to the Blackcomb Glacier.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate, the East Col, onto the Spearhead Glacier, then skin and bootpack to the notch at the top.
lines.exit: Down the Blackcomb Glacier to Glacier Road, then to the Crystal or Excelerator chairs, or down to the valley.
hazards: A slide in a narrow couloir piles up deep. Its bottom third has released in storms (a 2024 report found the run full of avalanche debris).
Cornice at the notch.
Glacier: crevasses on the way up.

lines.name: Corona Bowl
lines.about: A big bowl off the ridge north of the Spearhead, down to the Blackcomb Glacier valley, popular with experienced skiers. A group was caught by an avalanche here while getting ready to climb.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate, the East Col and the Spearhead Glacier, then skin north to the top of the bowl.
lines.exit: Down to the Blackcomb Glacier and Glacier Road, then the Crystal or Excelerator chairs, or the valley.
hazards: Big open slope: a slide here can be large.
Glacier: crevasses on the way up.

lines.name: Spearhead Glacier
lines.about: North-facing glacier runs from the head of the Spearhead Glacier, with lots of lines to skier's left and right, and more off the Spearhead Shoulder to the east.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate, up to the Spearhead col, a descending traverse, then a bootpack through Guides Notch to the head of the glacier.
lines.exit: Most groups skin back up to the ridge and ski Husume or Corona Bowl to the Blackcomb Glacier and Glacier Road.
hazards: Big crevasses: glacier gear (rope, harness) and the training to use it.
Crevasses decide which lines you can ski: they change every season.

lines.name: Phalanx Mountain (the Stairmaster)
lines.about: Lines off Phalanx Mountain back down to the Blackcomb Glacier. The bowl south-west of the summit gives about 250 m of skiing at 35 to 40°. The way up is the Stairmaster, a steep bootpack couloir of about 160 m to the summit.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate, the Spearhead col and the Spearhead Glacier, then bootpack the Stairmaster couloir to the notch between Phalanx's two summits.
lines.exit: Down to the Blackcomb Glacier and Glacier Road, then the Crystal or Excelerator chairs. Or the Phalanx Glacier and the Poop Chutes to Glacier Road.
hazards: Steep, narrow bootpack: sluffs and anyone above you come down the same couloir.
Cornices on the summit ridge.
Glacier on the way: crevasses.

lines.name: Poop Chutes
lines.about: Long chutes from the ridge north of Corona Bowl (toward Phalanx Mountain) down to Glacier Road: about 700 m down.
lines.access: From the Spearhead Glacier, skin north past Corona Bowl to the top. The way up isn't well documented: go with someone who knows it.
lines.exit: The chutes end on Glacier Road: follow it to the Crystal or Excelerator chairs, or the valley.
hazards: In 2021 two size 3 avalanches here killed one person and injured at least two others.
Long, narrow chutes that funnel any slide.

lines.name: Decker Mountain, north face
lines.about: The steep north face of Decker Mountain, above the small lake north of it: a very steep start (over 50°) through the cornices, then about 350 m of open slope. Several ways in; the west end is extreme (60°, cliffs). Named lines on Decker's north side include Chisel Chute, the Fingers, the 9th Hole and Decker Main; the Cham Chutes come down from the Spearhead col.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate and the East Col, down toward the lake north of Decker, round the foot of the north face and up its easier north-east slope to the summit plateau.
lines.exit: Skin back up to the East Col, ski the Blackcomb Glacier, then Glacier Road.
hazards: Huge cornices: the weakest spot is the small break in the summit plateau next to the high point.
Over 50° at the top.
Glaciers on the way: crevasses.

lines.name: Decker Glacier
lines.about: The long, more open run on Decker: north down the Decker Glacier to Decker Lake. Good for laps. Steeper lines on the same side: Chisel Chute, the Fingers, the 9th Hole (through corniced ground off the summit) and Decker Main.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate, over the East Col, down past Circle Lake to Decker Lake, then skin up to the top. About 2 to 3 hours.
lines.exit: Over the col between Decker and Disease Ridge, then a contouring traverse round Disease Ridge back to the bottom of 7th Heaven.
hazards: Crevasses on the glacier, worst early in the season: rope and harness.
Overhanging cornices on several slopes.
Busy: watch the ascent track, it crosses below other groups' lines.

lines.name: Spearhead Traverse
lines.about: The classic hut-to-hut ski traverse from Blackcomb to Whistler round the Spearhead and Fitzsimmons Ranges: about 35 km over 13 glaciers, usually 2 to 3 days with the Kees and Claire Hut on the way. Avalanche Canada rates it Complex.
lines.access: The Garibaldi Park gate on the Blackcomb Glacier, then up to the East Col.
lines.exit: Over Singing Pass and down the Singing Pass trail to Whistler Village.
hazards: Complex avalanche terrain the whole way: plan each slope with the day's forecast.
Many glaciers: crevasse gear and training.
Hard to bail out once past Decker: carry what you need to spend a night out.

resorts.name: Revelstoke Mountain Resort
resorts.emergency: Emergency outside the boundary: 911 (Revelstoke Search and Rescue). Resort dispatch and patrol: 250-814-5055.
rules: Past the rope it's the backcountry: no ski patrol, no avalanche control, and a rescue can take a long time. Many spots have no phone signal.
Everyone needs a transceiver, a probe, a shovel and skins, and Avalanche Skills Training 1 (AST 1) or the same.
Coming back through the resort: be back inside the boundary by 3:45 pm. After that the groomers, some on winch cables, are on the runs.
Tell someone your route and when you'll be back, and never go alone.
Stay off the cat skiing tenure south of the resort.

gates.name: Sub Peak gate
gates.note: Where the resort boundary rope meets the ridge south of Sub Peak. Get there from the top of the Stoke chair along the ridge (the Sub Peak hike). From here a skin track follows the ridge east toward Montana Peak, above South Bowl and Montana Bowl.

lines.name: South Bowl
lines.about: The closest slackcountry to the lifts: a short skin past the gate, then open slopes and trees facing south-west, back toward the resort's south side.
lines.access: Through the gate below Sub Peak, then a short skin east along the ridge to the top of the bowl.
lines.exit: Traverse west at the bottom of the bowl back inside the boundary, near the bottom of Jalapeno and the Ninja Traverse.
hazards: Sun-baked south-west slopes: wet slides in the afternoon and in spring.
Cornices on the ridge above.
Easy to drift too far down: stay high enough to traverse back.

lines.name: Montana ridge, south faces
lines.about: Longer open lines off the ridge between Sub Peak and Montana Peak, south-west facing, ending in the trees above the traverse back to the resort.
lines.access: Through the gate below Sub Peak, then about 2 km east on the ridge skin track.
lines.exit: At the bottom, take the long traverse west (the way back on the map) to Devil's Club inside the resort. It's mostly downhill but long; skins help in deep snow.
hazards: Big open slopes above the trees: avalanche terrain, and slides run into the trees below.
Wet slides on sunny afternoons.
Cornices on the ridge.

lines.name: Montana Bowl
lines.about: The big alpine bowl at the far end of the ridge, below Montana Peak. Steep at the top, then a long run out west under the ridge.
lines.access: Through the gate below Sub Peak, then all the way east on the ridge skin track (about 2.5 km, 20-40 minutes) to the top of the bowl.
lines.exit: Ski out west under the ridge to the long traverse back to Devil's Club inside the resort.
hazards: Steep alpine start with cornices: the most serious line here.
Wind slabs on the lee slopes.
A long way from the resort if something goes wrong.

lines.name: Montana Trees
lines.about: Spaced trees below Montana Bowl, cut by an old cat skiing operation. Steady fall line down to about 1,750 m.
lines.access: Through the gate below Sub Peak, east along the ridge skin track, then down into the top of the trees below Montana Bowl.
lines.exit: Put skins on at the bottom and skin back up north-west (about 170 m up) to the resort side, near the bottom of Jalapeno.
hazards: The trees are below big avalanche paths: don't stop under open slopes.
You must skin out: leave time to be back by 3:45 pm.
Tree wells in deep snow.

resorts.name: Whitewater
resorts.emergency: Emergency outside the boundary: 911 (Nelson Search and Rescue). There's no phone signal on most of the mountain. Dispatch: 250-354-4944 ext. 136.
rules: Past the boundary there's no ski patrol and no avalanche control, and you pay for your own rescue.
Check in with Whitewater's Snow Safety Patrol before you go out, with your route and return time.
You sign the Backcountry Access Waiver with your lift ticket (single-ride tickets are sold for backcountry access).
No skinning or hiking up inside the boundary, before, during or after hours. Uphill only on the signed ascent route outside the boundary.
Everyone needs a transceiver, a probe and a shovel (they rent kits at the base) and avalanche training. There's a transceiver park near the day lodge.

gates.name: Silver King gate
gates.note: At the top of the Silver King chair. Leads north to White Queen and east over the ridge to Five Mile Basin.

gates.name: Claim Jumper gate
gates.note: At the top of Claim Jumper (Glory Ridge chair). A short hike up the ridge leads to the Trash Chutes; from the bottom you ski back to the Glory lift.

gates.name: Powder Keg gate
gates.note: In Powder Keg Bowl, near the top of the Summit chair. The skin track goes east to the Prospector and Hummingbird, and on to Ymir.

lines.name: White Queen
lines.about: The classic Whitewater slackcountry lap: skin up White Queen from the Silver King gate and ski the trees and open slopes back down its south-west side to the resort.
lines.access: Through the Silver King gate, then about 45 minutes up the skin track along the ridge to the summit (2,180 m).
lines.exit: The run ends on the Silver King ski way: follow it back to the Silver King chair.
hazards: Open slopes near the top hold wind slabs.
Gullies in the lower trees.
Don't drop off the north side: it goes away from the resort.

lines.name: Five Mile Basin
lines.about: One drainage east of the resort: from the ridge above Half Dome, north-west facing slopes and trees down into Five Mile Basin, then skin back out.
lines.access: Through the Silver King gate, then the skin track east up the ridge toward Half Dome (about 300 m up).
lines.exit: Skin back up the zig-zag track to the ridge and return west to the Silver King gate. Don't follow the creek down: it goes away from the resort.
hazards: Slopes up to about 35°, open at the top.
You have to skin out: leave time and energy.
Avalanche paths come down from Half Dome and Ymir on the far side.

lines.name: Ymir Bowl, from Ymir Mountain
lines.about: From the top of Ymir Mountain (2,398 m), the big bowl on its north-west side back down toward the resort's east edge. Steep alpine skiing.
lines.access: Through the Powder Keg gate, then the skin track east past the Prospector and Hummingbird and up Ymir's west ridge (about 450 m up).
lines.exit: The bowl drains west to the creek on the resort's east side: follow it out to the Silver King chair.
hazards: Steep (up to about 45°), open and corniced at the top.

Exposed to wind: hard to find the way in a whiteout.

lines.name: The Prospector, north side
lines.about: A short climb from the Powder Keg gate to the Prospector (2,127 m), then its north side straight back down into the resort.
lines.access: Through the Powder Keg gate, then the Prospector skin track east (about 170 m up).
lines.exit: Ends back inside the resort: ski out to the Silver King chair.

resorts.name: RED Mountain
resorts.emergency: Emergency outside the boundary: 911 (Rossland Search and Rescue).
rules: Backcountry travelers are on their own: no ski patrol and no avalanche control outside the boundary.
Only for experienced skiers and riders with avalanche training. Carry a transceiver, a probe and a shovel; a helmet and first aid kit are recommended.
Most terrain past the gate leads AWAY from the resort, to Big Sheep Creek or the old Cascade Highway, many km from the base. Know your way back before you drop.
Kirkup's cat skiing terrain is in-bounds and swept by ski patrol: it isn't part of this layer.

gates.note: At the fork of Silver Sheep and Rino's Run, behind Granite Mountain. White Wolf Ridge is a short hike from the gate and Record Ridge is to the south-west (left).

gates.note: RED says Mount Roberts is about a 45-minute hike from Silver Sheep in Paradise Basin.

lines.name: White Wolf Ridge
lines.about: Simple terrain: open trees from the ridge just above the gate, back down to Silver Sheep and Rino's Run.
lines.access: Through the gate, then a short hike north-west up the ridge.
lines.exit: The glades come back down to Silver Sheep and Rino's Run inside the resort.
hazards: Don't drop west: the west-facing side leads to Big Sheep Creek, about 40 km from the ski area.
Simple terrain, but still not controlled.

lines.name: Record Peak, east bowl
lines.about: The east face of Record Peak (2,113 m) is a steep, open bowl. The north face is complex, steep and corniced.
lines.access: Through the gate, then south-west along Record Ridge to the summit (about 200 m up).
lines.exit: From the bottom of the bowl, skin back north-east up to the gate (about 200 m up). All the terrain beyond leads away from the resort, to Big Sheep Creek or the Cascade Highway: it's easy to get lost.
hazards: Steep, open bowl: avalanche terrain.

lines.name: Mount Roberts, north chutes
lines.about: Steep (about 50° at the summit), with several couloirs from the top of Mount Roberts (1,980 m). The north-facing chutes are complex, steep and corniced.
lines.access: About a 45-minute hike from Silver Sheep in Paradise Basin, south up to the summit.
lines.exit: The north side comes back down into the bottom of Paradise Basin: traverse to the Paradise chair. Some terrain leads down to the Cascade Highway, about 10 km from the ski area.
hazards: Very steep, corniced chutes.
A fall in a couloir is serious.
Lines to the south and east end at the Cascade Highway, far from RED.

resorts.name: Fernie Alpine Resort
resorts.forecast: Avalanche Canada, Lizard Range and Flathead
resorts.emergency: Emergency outside the boundary: 911 (Fernie Search and Rescue). Resort dispatch: 250-423-2426.
rules: Ski tourers must leave the resort through one of the 4 backcountry access points: Mammoth Droppings and Lost Boys Pass (south), the top of Snake Ridge (north) and the Polar Peak saddle (west).
An access point is only open when the lift or terrain leading to it is open. You need a valid lift ticket or pass.
Uphill travel inside the resort is never allowed.
There's no avalanche control and no ski patrol outside the boundary.
Don't go out after the lifts close: cats, winches and avalanche control may be working. Coming back in, follow all resort signs.

gates.name: Polar Peak saddle access
gates.note: West boundary, on the ridge north of Polar Peak (Polar Peak chair; open only when the chair is). Leads to Polaris Bowl, with the backcountry transceiver gate.

gates.name: Top of Snake Ridge access
gates.note: North boundary, at the end of the Cedar High Traverse on top of Snake Ridge. Leads to upper Fish Bowl.

gates.name: Lost Boys Pass access
gates.note: South boundary. Leads to Mammoth Head and Lost Boys Pass. No line drawn yet: we couldn't find where the usual lines go. Locals warn Lost Boys Pass is aptly named: it's easy to end up in the wrong drainage.

gates.name: Mammoth Droppings access
gates.note: South boundary. Leads to Mongolia Ridge (and Siberia and Mongolia bowls, a short skin from Timber Bowl). No line drawn yet: we couldn't find a reliable description of the lines.

lines.name: Polaris Bowl
lines.about: From the Polar Peak saddle, west down Polaris Bowl to the valley the Thunder Meadows cabin route calls Easy Street (about 800 m down). It's the start of a tour, not a lap: the valley is on the far side of the ridge from the resort.
lines.access: Ride the Polar Peak chair (it opens only on some days), ski to the saddle north of Polar Peak and go through the backcountry transceiver gate.
lines.exit: There's no easy way back to the resort: from the valley, skin up to the Thunder Meadows cabin (the usual plan), or skin all the way back up to the saddle. Plan it as a backcountry tour.
hazards: The route crosses many slide paths: a deathtrap when the avalanche danger is high.
Steep, open slopes under the ridge.
You end up far from the resort, on the wrong side of the ridge.

lines.name: Upper Fish Bowl
lines.about: From the ridge above the top of Snake Ridge, north-east down the upper Fish Bowl to the old road that leads back into the resort.
lines.access: Through the access point at the top of Snake Ridge (end of the Cedar High Traverse), then skin west up the ridge (about 230 m).
lines.exit: At the bottom, follow Red Tree Road east back into the resort.
hazards: The traverse across Fish Bowl and 2000 Foot Ridge crosses steep avalanche terrain: ski patrol closes it when the danger is high.
Steep (up to about 45°) near the top.
Don't follow the creek past the road: it leads away from the resort.

resorts.name: Cypress Mountain
rules: Cypress is inside a BC Park. From November 1 to May 31, backcountry users must go through the ski area on the Backcountry Access Corridor (BAC), marked by green round signs. The trails beyond are marked by red poles.
Get a free backcountry access tag at the Brown Bag Room in Black Mountain Lodge before you go.
BC Parks strongly discourages winter travel along the Howe Sound Crest Trail past Bowen Lookout. Both lines here are past it.
Never duck the rope at the top of the Sky Chair: the west side drops into the Montizambert drainage, with cliffs and a waterfall.
Everyone needs a transceiver, a probe and a shovel, and avalanche training. Tell someone your plan.

gates.name: Backcountry Access Corridor
gates.note: The marked BC Parks route through the ski area, past Bowen Lookout to the Howe Sound Crest Trail and Mount Strachan. Get the free tag at Black Mountain Lodge first.

lines.name: Christmas Gully
lines.about: The gully between Mount Strachan's two summits, skied west down to Strachan Meadows on the Howe Sound Crest Trail. Short, steep and narrow.
lines.access: From the top of the Sky Chair area, up to the col between the summits of Mount Strachan (outside the ski area: follow the BAC and the red poles, never duck the rope).
lines.exit: From Strachan Meadows, follow the Howe Sound Crest Trail south back to Bowen Lookout and the ski area. It's mostly flat with short climbs.
hazards: A gully: a terrain trap where even a small slide piles up deep. A skier who triggered a slide here hit trees and broke a femur; the rescue took a helicopter.
Steep at the top (40°+).
Don't drift north or west of the gully: the slopes drop toward Montizambert Creek and cliffs.

lines.name: Strachan south summit, west face
lines.about: From the south summit of Mount Strachan, the open face skied north-west down to Strachan Meadows. OpenStreetMap marks it "NOT IN BOUNDS".
lines.access: Up the south summit of Mount Strachan, above the top of the Sky Chair, on the BAC route (never duck the rope).
lines.exit: From Strachan Meadows, follow the Howe Sound Crest Trail south back to Bowen Lookout and the ski area.
hazards: Open slope: avalanche terrain, with trees below.
Two hikers caught in a slide were carried into the Christmas Gully area behind Mount Strachan.
Coastal snow changes fast: rain crusts and wet slides.

resorts.name: Mount Seymour
resorts.emergency: Emergency: 911 (North Shore Rescue). Mt Seymour Resorts: 604-986-2261.
rules: There's no lift-served gate: BC Parks sets a ski-touring up-track each winter (mid-December to March 31) from the kiosk at the north end of parking lot P4, near the Mystery Peak chair.
Navigate by the marker poles (orange bamboo, red plastic). Trail conditions and the avalanche rating are posted at the kiosk.
Backcountry users park in P1 or lower P5. Post your plan and return time on your dashboard if you park overnight in P1.
BC Parks: the backcountry here is extremely rugged and the weather changes suddenly. Check avalanche.ca and leave a trip plan.

gates.name: BC Parks kiosk, lot P4
gates.note: Start of the Mount Seymour Backcountry Access Trail. 7 km return to the saddle between First and Second Pump; about 3 hours on skis.

lines.name: Mount Seymour Backcountry Access Trail to Pump Peak
lines.about: The BC Parks up-track along the west side of the ski area to the saddle between First and Second Pump (Pump Peak, 1,407 m), then back down the same way.
lines.access: From the kiosk at lot P4, skin up the marked trail (about 370 m up).
lines.exit: Come back down the same trail. Stay on the marked route: don't drop into the gullies on either side.
hazards: Past Pump Peak toward Tim Jones and Mount Seymour the ridge gets steep and corniced.
The gullies off the sides lead into the Seymour River or Indian Arm drainages, far from the road.
Fog is common: easy to lose the poles.

resorts.name: Sun Peaks
resorts.emergency: Ski Patrol emergency: 250-578-5521 (they do NOT help outside the boundary; call 911). Grooming (winch cat locations): 250-319-5028.
rules: There are two gated exits for prepared backcountry guests: at the end of First Saddle and at Second Saddle.
Outside the boundary there's no patrol and no avalanche control. Phone signal is poor or none.
No uphill travel (skinning, hiking, snowshoeing) inside the ski area boundary.
Coming back through the resort: be inside by 3:45 pm, because winch cats run on the slopes.
AST 1 or the same is highly recommended. Don't go alone, and tell someone where you're going and when you'll be back.

gates.name: First Saddle gate
gates.note: At the end of First Saddle, near the entrance to Main Face and Offset. Leads west onto the open slopes below Mount Tod's summit (2,131 m). No line drawn: we found no published description of the lines.

gates.name: Second Saddle gate
gates.note: Between Skunk and the top of the old West Bowl T-bar. Leads west, outside the boundary. No line drawn: we found no published description of the lines.

resorts.name: Lake Louise Ski Resort
resorts.forecast: Avalanche Canada, Banff Yoho Kootenay (Parks Canada)
resorts.emergency: Emergency: 911 (Parks Canada visitor safety). There's no phone signal in most of the backcountry here.
rules: This is Banff National Park: outside the ski area there's no patrol and no avalanche control. Read the Parks Canada avalanche forecast first.
Uphill travel inside the ski area is only allowed on the signed route from the Ski Out toward Temple and Skoki.
Everyone needs a transceiver, a probe, a shovel and skins, plus avalanche training. Yamnuska runs guided tours into these bowls from the resort.

gates.name: Temple exit (Skoki up-track)
gates.note: By Temple Lodge, at the bottom of the Larch area. Skin tracks leave here east to Purple Bowl (Purple Mound route) and north up the Skoki ski route toward Boulder Pass and Redoubt.

lines.name: Purple Bowl, from Purple Mound
lines.about: From the top of Purple Mound (2,622 m), north down Purple Bowl, the valley between Wolverine Ridge and Unity Peak, back to the up-track.
lines.access: From Temple, skin east around the north end of Wolverine Ridge into Purple Bowl, keep just right of the creek and climb the ramp at the end of the valley to the summit (about 600 m up, 2-3 hours). A shorter, steeper way goes up from the ski area through the col between Purple Mound and Wolverine Ridge.
lines.exit: Follow the up-track back west around Wolverine Ridge to Temple, then ride the lifts or take the Ski Out.
hazards: Slopes below the summit and the ramp are avalanche terrain.
Sun-crust on south slopes in spring.
Wind slabs on the lee side of Wolverine Ridge.

lines.name: Redoubt Bowl
lines.about: The bowl on the west side of Redoubt Mountain (2,902 m), on the way to Boulder Pass. A popular ski descent; the line follows the summer route of the peak, so it's only a guide.
lines.access: From Temple, skin up the Skoki ski route north, then east up Redoubt's west side (about 800 m up).
lines.exit: Ski back down to the Skoki route and follow it south to Temple.
hazards: Big alpine terrain above the Skoki route: slides can reach the track below.
Steep near the top, with cliffs.
A full ski tour: plan a whole day.

resorts.name: Shames Mountain
resorts.emergency: Emergency outside the boundary: 911 (Terrace Search and Rescue). Shames Ski Patrol only looks after people inside the boundary.
rules: Shames' out-of-bounds terrain isn't patrolled: the ski patrol only covers the marked ski area.
Use the beacon check gate before you leave, and carry a transceiver, a probe and a shovel (Shames rents them, plus touring gear).
The resort recommends Avalanche Skills Training, up-to-date gear and the fitness to get yourself out, and reading the avalanche forecast before you leave the boundary.
Shames sells single-ride tickets and an uphill season pass for backcountry users.

gates.name: Beacon check gate, top of the Red T-Bar
gates.note: Going left from the top of the T-bar drops into the out-of-bounds glades, called some of the best slackcountry in North America. From the top of the ski area people also skin toward the Dome and North Bowl. No lines drawn yet: we found no reliable description of where they go.
